name: How do you calculate the rough opening dimensions for a new door?

mainEntity.name: How do you calculate the rough opening dimensions for a new door?

acceptedAnswer.text: To determine the rough opening, measure the actual door slab and add 2 inches to its width and 2 to 2.5 inches to its height. For example, a standard 32-inch by 80-inch interior door needs a rough framed opening of roughly 34 inches by 82.5 inches. This extra space accounts for the 3/4-inch jamb material on both sides and leaves clearance to shim, level, and square the jamb. You must also account for finished flooring thickness: if framing over subfloor before hardwood or tile is laid, add height so the door clears the final floor level.
acceptedAnswer.description: Add 2 inches to the door's width and 2 to 2.5 inches to its height to allow room for the jambs, leveling shims, and finished flooring.
